results.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code | alphaXiv
results.content:
Related systems provide context rather than controlled baselines. SceneCraft is a text-to-Blender scene agent that uses visual feedback, and Articraft builds articulated objects with a task-specific SDK and geometric validation. The difference claimed here is breadth and shared infrastructure, not a demonstrated head-to-head win.

Qualitative examples of outputs without and with the harness, plus refinement sequences [...] We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. First, we construct 3DCodeVerse-2M, a large-scale curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code. We build this corpus by collecting open-source data, converting specialized representations, and generating new programs with coding agents. Each program is packaged with the source files and associated assets required for execution in its declared environment, along with available descriptions and verification records. Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi-agent [...] View Paper

## AI Overview

Getting 3D code to run is the easy part. A script can build without errors and still yield an asset with missing, misplaced, or colliding parts, and fixing those defects by hand does not scale. 3DCodeVerse, the system described in this paper, hands the checking and repair to agents that plan, build, measure, render, judge, and revise the code with no human steering the revisions. The authors argue that this loop is what makes high-quality 3D programs achievable without human feedback.

The clearest payoff is a controlled comparison. On a 60-prompt set of 3D objects, the same Claude Opus 5.5 backbone was preferred 90% of the time when run inside the 3DCodeVerse harness versus inside Claude Design.

results.content:
3DCodeVerse: How to Code Your Own 3D Universe  
  
Build a realistic 3D world without ever touching a modeling tool. The project named 3D Code Verse gives coding agents a complete workshop where they can write, run, and fix the actual scripts that make objects, scenes, and graphics come alive. Instead of guessing at images, these programs are measured against real physics and rendered views, so the system knows exactly when a joint is broken or a light is flat. It then repairs the code automatically, turning every failure into better training data for the next model. This turns 3D creation from a black box into a transparent, code-based workflow you can actually inspect and improve.  
  
Open source: gaoypeng/3dcodeverse  
  
Follow for more open source project drops.
